title: The Organization as an Operating System
summary: Every organized group runs an OS: implicit or explicit rules for who decides, who does, and how resources flow.
body:
Org OS: the operating system of any organization — nonprofits, clubs, churches, teams. Scheduling volunteers, managing shared resources, and keeping the mission running on goodwill and structure.

Every organized group runs an OS: implicit or explicit rules for who decides, who does, and how resources flow. Making it explicit — writing it down — is the single highest-leverage upgrade.

title: Volunteer Scheduling
summary: Volunteers are preemptible processes: they can vanish.
body:
Volunteers are preemptible processes: they can vanish. Design for it — redundancy (two-deep leadership), graceful degradation (core functions covered first), and appreciation as the scheduler's priority boost.

Context: this record is part of the Org Os catalog — org os: the operating system of any organization — nonprofits, clubs, churches, teams.
facts: Two-deep: every role has a backup
No guilt-tripping: volunteers aren't threads you own

program.code:
# Round-robin scheduler: the OS concept behind fair task sharing
from collections import deque
def round_robin(tasks, quantum=2):
    q = deque((name, burst) for name, burst in tasks)
    t = 0
    while q:
        name, burst = q.popleft()
        run = min(quantum, burst)
        t += run; burst -= run
        print(f"t={t:3d}  {name} ran {run} (remaining {burst})")
        if burst: q.append((name, burst))
round_robin([("email",5),("report",3),("calls",4)])

summary: Meetings are expensive syscalls into everyone's time.
